title.narrative: Ipas/SRHR "Increasing access to justice and care including safe abortion"
Ipas/SRHR "Öka tillgången till rättvisa och vård inklusive säker abort "

description.narrative:
Project Goal:
Women and girls can exercise their sexual and reproductive rights, including the right to access safe abortion without stigma or revictimization, especially in cases of SGBV.
Objective 1: Improve community support for SGBV survivors and reduce stigma surrounding their right to access safe abortion.
Objective 2: Build the capacity of legal gatekeepers in Bolivia to facilitate and advocate for SRHR, including safe abortion for SGBV survivors.

Projektet syftar till att förverkliga genomförandet av Montevideo-konsensus (Intensifiera arbetet för sexuella och reproduktiva rättigheter för alla) i Bolivia genom att institutionalisera säkra, högkvalitativa, hållbara abort- och preventivmedelstjänster. En stark komponent i detta arbete är frågan om att främja Mänskliga Rättigheters perspektivet i tillgång till kvalitativ abortvård i landet.

The project aims to realize the implementation of the Montevideo Consensus in Bolivia by institutionalizing safe, high-quality, sustainable abortion and contraception services. A strong component of this work is the issue of promoting the right perspective in relation to access to qualitative abortion care in the country.

Results Achieved 2025 The intervention was carried out with 12 Violence Prevention Networks in educational communities (UE Mercedes Fiengo, Santo Tomás, COMVIFAC, Elizardo Pérez, Cobija B, Guido Villagómez, Juan Misael Saracho, Tuksupaya, Andrés Ibáñez, Efraín Vargas Paz and El Paraíso A). These networks strengthened coordination among students, teachers, and parents, and implemented prevention actions and referrals to institutions such as DNA and EPI, with a total of seven cases attended and referred during the period. Information and awareness activities reached 10,426 members of the educational community.
In coordination with the Fundación para el Periodismo, efforts were made to promote the destigmatization of media coverage related to sexual violence, abortion, and SRHR through training sessions and the production of informative articles. The training A new and urgent approach: sexual violence and its consequences enabled outreach through radio stations with coverage in rural areas (Erbol, Splendid, Kancha Parlaspa, Líder, PIO XII, Ichilo, Andina, and Méndez), disseminating accurate information in local languages and cultural contexts. REDACTORA, composed of seven young journalists, was consolidated and went on to develop and implement an advocacy plan through written media.
The sustained campaign Sin peros en la lengua reached 150,182 people. In the health sector, the ProChoice
Providers Network was strengthened, composed of 41 physicians and nurses committed to providing safe services to women, particularly survivors of sexual violence. During the period, 2,324 women received care, including cases involving advanced gestationalage abortions and contraceptive services. The experience of trained professionals was shared with CLACAI, promoting regional alliances.
The Gender Unit of the National Police replicated the training among its peers. Likewise, Law students from UMSA strengthened their capacities to support and defend survivors of sexual violence. The Network of Lawyers, committed to the rights of women and girls, successfully provided legal defense to six women during the period.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
